A.claim: Whenever 3|x, 3|y and 3|z, A^x + B^y = C^z has no positive solutions; in particular no Beal counterexample has such a signature, including the Fermat cubic (3,3,3).

B.claim: Exactly one of A, B, C is even in any Beal counterexample. Not two, by pairwise coprimality; not zero, since two odd bases force C^z even.

combine.instructions: Would combining these two candidates produce a genuinely NEW attack (not a reword of either)?

level 3: the combination could close an infinite family
